noteBlocks.lede: Everything around you is built from atoms, and every atom is built from just three particles. Where those particles sit, what charge they carry and how the electrons are arranged explains almost everything else in chemistry: which ions elements form, and how they bond.

Write the electronic configuration of atoms and ions up to calcium.

noteBlocks.md: An atom is far too small to see: hundreds of thousands of them would fit across the width of one hair. Yet chemists know exactly what is inside one. This lesson opens an atom up, counts what is in it, and shows why the way its electrons are arranged matters so much.

noteBlocks.md:
Every atom is built from **protons**, **neutrons** and **electrons**. Their charges and masses are **relative**, measured against the proton: a proton has charge **+1** and mass **1**, a neutron charge **0** and mass **1**, an electron charge **−1** and mass **1/1840**.
Keep the **+** on the proton's charge, and write the electron's mass as **1/1840**, not 'almost zero'.

noteBlocks.title: Why the nucleus holds nearly all the mass
noteBlocks.md: A proton or a neutron has about 1840 times the mass of an electron. However many electrons an atom has, they add almost nothing to its mass, so nearly all of it sits in the nucleus, even though the nucleus is tiny next to the whole atom.

noteBlocks.prompt: Using the particle table above, why is nearly all of an atom's mass in its nucleus?
options: protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1, and an electron only 1/1840
the nucleus takes up most of the space in the atom
electrons have no mass at all
noteBlocks.answer: protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1, and an electron only 1/1840
noteBlocks.explain: The heavy particles are in the nucleus. The nucleus itself is tiny, not large, and electrons do have mass: just 1/1840 of a proton's.

noteBlocks.md:
The **atomic number** is the number of **protons** in an atom. Protons only: bringing electrons or neutrons into the definition loses the mark.
The **mass number** counts the **protons and neutrons together**: the two added up, in one atom.
In an **atom** the number of electrons equals the number of protons, so the positive and negative charges cancel and the atom has **no overall charge**.

noteBlocks.title: Where this mark goes
noteBlocks.md: In Summer 2025 few candidates at either tier gave atomic number exactly. Many added electrons to the protons, some added neutrons, and every extra particle cost the mark.

noteBlocks.prompt: Which of these is the definition of atomic number?
options: the number of protons in an atom
the number of protons and electrons in an atom
the number of protons and neutrons in one atom
noteBlocks.answer: the number of protons in an atom
noteBlocks.explain: Protons only. Protons and neutrons together is the mass number, and adding electrons is the slip the examiners penalised.

noteBlocks.prompt: A lithium atom, with 3 protons and 3 electrons, loses one of its electrons. What is left?
options: a lithium ion with a 1+ charge
a lithium ion with a 1− charge
noteBlocks.answer: a lithium ion with a 1+ charge
noteBlocks.explain: The protons decide the element, and there are still 3, so it is still lithium. With 3 protons and only 2 electrons the charge is 3 − 2 = 1+.

noteBlocks.md:
The Data Leaflet gives each element's **atomic number** (bottom) and **relative atomic mass** (top). For the elements up to calcium, except chlorine, the top number is the **mass number** of the common atom.
**The question.** How many protons, neutrons and electrons does an aluminium atom have? **[3]**
**Step 1 — protons.** The atomic number is 13, so **13 protons**.
**Step 2 — neutrons.** Mass number take away atomic number: 27 − 13 = **14 neutrons**.

noteBlocks.prompt: Finish the aluminium example. An aluminium atom has 13 protons and 14 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
noteBlocks.explain: 13. An atom has no overall charge, so its electrons equal its protons. 27, the mass number, is the classic slip: the mass number counts no electrons at all.

noteBlocks.md:
Electrons fill **shells** from the inside out. For the first 20 elements the first shell holds up to **2**, the second up to **8**, the third up to **8**, and anything left starts the **fourth**.
The **electronic configuration** lists the shells from the inside, separated by commas: sodium's 11 electrons are **2,8,1**; calcium's 20 are **2,8,8,2**. The numbers always add up to the number of electrons.

noteBlocks.title: Why the arrangement matters
noteBlocks.md: The electrons in the **outer shell** decide how an atom reacts. Elements with the same number of outer electrons behave alike, which is why they share a group of the Periodic Table, and why the lessons on ions and bonding start from the outer shell.

noteBlocks.title: GCSE Chemistry - Electronic Structure (2027/28 exams)
noteBlocks.why: A second run through filling shells and drawing configurations. Cognito calls it electronic structure; CCEA's word is electronic configuration.

noteBlocks.prompt: Write the electronic configuration of a potassium atom, atomic number 19.
noteBlocks.explain: 2,8,8,1. The third shell stops at 8 for these elements, so the nineteenth electron starts the fourth shell. 2,8,9 is the slip to avoid.

noteBlocks.md:
An **ion** is a charged particle made when an atom **gains or loses electrons**. The protons never change, so the charge is **protons minus electrons**.
Oxygen has 8 protons. Gaining 2 electrons gives it 10, so the charge is 8 − 10 = −2, written 2−: the oxide ion, $\ce{O^{2-}}$, configuration **2,8**. Magnesium has 12 protons; losing 2 electrons leaves 10, a charge of 2+: $\ce{Mg^{2+}}$, also **2,8**.
Work out an ion's configuration from its **electrons**, never from its atomic number.

noteBlocks.explain: 16 + 2 = 18. A negative ion has gained electrons, so add them. Its configuration is then 2,8,8.

noteBlocks.md:
Atoms of different elements can join by chemical bonds. The result is a **compound**: **two or more elements chemically combined**. Magnesium oxide is magnesium and oxygen chemically combined.
Each part of that definition carries weight: say **elements**, not atoms; say **two or more**, not 'several'; and say **chemically** combined, because a mixture is not.

noteBlocks.prompt: Which of these is the definition of a compound?
options: two or more elements chemically combined
two or more atoms joined together
two or more elements mixed together
noteBlocks.answer: two or more elements chemically combined
noteBlocks.explain: Elements, two or more, chemically combined. 'Atoms' would also fit a molecule of a single element, such as oxygen, and 'mixed' describes a mixture.

Describe the structure of an atom of magnesium, $\ce{^{24}_{12}Mg}$.
In your answer you should include:

indicativeContent.point: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus, at the centre of the atom.
Electrons are in shells around the nucleus.
A proton has relative charge +1 and relative mass 1.
A neutron has relative charge 0 and relative mass 1.
An electron has relative charge −1 and relative mass 1/1840.
Magnesium-24 has 12 protons, 12 neutrons and 12 electrons, arranged 2,8,2.
The atom has no overall charge because its protons and electrons are equal in number.

equal number of protons and electrons

scheme.for: a banded answer covering where the particles are (protons and neutrons in the nucleus, electrons in shells), their relative charges and masses, the 12 protons, 12 neutrons and 12 electrons of magnesium-24 with the configuration 2,8,2, and equal numbers of protons and electrons as the reason for no overall charge
scheme.examinerNote: A point contradicted elsewhere in the answer is not counted. Capital letters and full stops are part of the within-band judgement.

hints: Work through the four bullet points in order.
Use numbers: 12, 12, 12 and 2,8,2.
parts.workedSolution: An atom of magnesium has a small central nucleus, which contains the protons and the neutrons. The electrons are in shells around the nucleus. A proton has a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of 1. A neutron has no charge and a relative mass of 1. An electron has a relative charge of −1 and a relative mass of 1/1840, so nearly all the mass of the atom is in the nucleus. Magnesium has atomic number 12, so this atom has 12 protons and 12 electrons, and it has 24 − 12 = 12 neutrons. The electrons are arranged 2,8,2: two in the first shell, eight in the second and two in the third. The atom has no overall charge because its protons and electrons are equal in number, so the positive and negative charges cancel.

findTheMistake.stem:
Niamh is asked: 'Give the electronic configuration of an oxygen atom [1] and of the oxide ion, O²⁻ [1].'
